reports.title: SP1 Audit Report: Appendix
reports.description: Security-minded appendix written during the initial KALOS audit of the SP1 Core zkVM, describing the constraint system (interactions/lookup argument, offline memory checking, ALU chips, precompile syscalls, CPU chip, memory/program chips) with completeness and soundness arguments and pointers for future auditors. It is a living document without an overall pinned revision; the only pinnable code reference is the shard public-values consistency check in the STARK verifier introduced by succinctlabs/sp1 PR #655.

reports.title: Veridise Auditing Report for SP1 (recursion circuits and sp1-contracts), V2
reports.description: Veridise manually re-audited the SP1 recursion circuits (recursion/compiler, recursion/program, recursion/circuit and the gnark-ffi Go code implementing BabyBear arithmetic and Poseidon2 over BN254) at commit 1049583, reviewed additional recursion changes at commit 6e968e3, and reviewed the Solidity verifier gateway contracts in sp1-contracts at commit 73c2a8d. The audit uncovered 19 issues, 5 of High severity (4 fixed, 1 acknowledged), 1 Medium, 2 Low, 3 Warning and 8 Informational.

Manual review of the recursive STARK verifier programs (core, compress, deferred, root verifiers, challenger, FRI) focusing on the diff since commits b6eac88, ab103ee and 02c6ea6, checking input validation, constraints and public-value commitments, and consistency with the non-recursive verifier and Plonky3 FRI. High findings V-SP1-VUL-001 (machine/{core,compress,deferred,root}.rs) and V-SP1-VUL-002 (challenger.rs); Medium V-SP1-VUL-006.
Confirmed fix of V-SP1-VUL-001 (shard index taken from public values) in src/machine/{core,compress,deferred,root}.rs only; V-SP1-VUL-002 in challenger.rs still open at this commit.

reports.title: SP1 V3 Audit Report
reports.description: Internal security review by rkm0959 of the SP1 v3 proving system: STARK prover/verifier Fiat-Shamir and cumulative-sum logic, the recursion circuits (challengers, bit decompositions, vk Merkle root, public-value propagation) and the syscall chip scopes. The report lists 14 issues with links to the fixing pull requests and commits in succinctlabs/sp1.

versions.coverage: Fix review of issue 10 [High]: the recursive shard verifier now asserts that the per-shard local cumulative sum is zero (PR #1531 head).
Fix review of issues 5 [Medium] and 6 [High]: cumulative sums are observed by the challenger after the permutation commitment and forced to zero for scopes without interactions (PR #1556 head).
Fix review of issue 3-2 [Low]: sample_bits/num2bits now use a canonical 31-bit decomposition (PR #1555 head). Issue 1-1 (full sponge state used as output) is reported unfixed.
Fix review of issue 1-2 [Medium]: MultiField32ChallengerVariable absorbs at rate 2 instead of overwriting the full width-3 sponge state (PR #1575 head).
Fix review of issue 13 [Informational]: execution_shard initialization in the core recursion program (PR #1576 head). Issue 12 [Informational] on committed_value_digest is reported unfixed.
Fix review of issue 7 [Medium]: exit_code is updated from every shard's public values (PR #1577 head).
Fix review of issue 7 [Medium]: follow-up commit asserting the final exit_code is zero (commit bc187d5bc referenced by the report).
Fix review of issue 13 [Informational]: execution_shard is set from the first proof that contains an execution shard (PR #1576 head).
Fix review of issue 7 [Medium]: exit_code propagated into compress public values before the digest is computed (PR #1577 head).
Issue 14 [Optimization]: felts_to_bn254_var uses CircuitFelt2Var instead of num2bits/bits2num (PR #1553 head). Only this function is discussed.
Fix review of issue 1-2 [Medium]: outer MultiField32Challenger configured with explicit width 3 / rate 2 constants (PR #1575 head). Only the outer challenger type is discussed.
Fix review of issue 3-2 [Low]: num2bits_v2_f range-checks the 31-bit decomposition against the BabyBear modulus (PR #1555 head). Only this function is discussed.

Fix review of issue 3-2 [Low]: redundant less_than_bb_modulus check removed from num2bits_f_circuit, whose canonicality is enforced by the gnark backend (PR #1555 head). Only this function is discussed.
Fix review of issue 11 [High]: accum constraint gated on when_not(is_first) instead of when_not(is_last) (PR #1482 head). Only this constraint is discussed.
Fix review of issues 5 [Medium] and 6 [High]: cumulative sums observed after permutation_commit and constrained to zero for scopes without interactions (PR #1556 head).
Fix review of issue 8 [Medium]: per-shard local cumulative sum check moved into the shard verifier as part of the syscall-chip scope rework (PR #1582 head).

Fix review of issue 9 [Medium]: prover-controlled chip_scopes field removed from ShardProof (PR #1642 head). Only this field is discussed.

reports.title: SP1 Design Review
reports.description: A one-engineer-day design-level review (not a code audit) of SP1's RV32IM standards compliance, focusing on the register/low-memory aliasing (addresses 0x0-0x1f), reserved memory regions, and the load/store instructions in the executor and prover crates. It concluded the aliasing is not a security vulnerability and recommended instruction-level checks as an enhancement.

versions.coverage: Design-level review only (explicitly not a code audit): RV32IM specification compliance, the register/low-memory aliasing at addresses 0x0-0x1f and reserved memory regions, focused mostly on the load and store instructions; correctness of implementation details and of other RV32IM instructions was out of scope.

Design-level review only (explicitly not a code audit): RV32IM specification compliance and the register/low-memory aliasing at addresses 0x0-0x1f, focused mostly on load and store instruction behaviour; soundness/completeness of the ZK proofs and circuits and correctness of implementation details were out of scope.

reports.title: SP1 V4 Audit Report
reports.description: Security audit by rkm0959 of the SP1 zkVM v4.0.0 release (commit 4a1dcea0749021ce6e2596bce5bb45f2def7a95c), performed 25 November to 13 December 2024 over three engineer-weeks and covering the new opcode-specific CPU/ECALL chips, the global interaction system, the recursion executor and the recursive verifier's verifying-key hashing. It also documents two v3-era soundness bugs (unchecked chip_ordering in the Rust STARK verifier and an is_complete bypass in the recursive verifier) that were fixed before v4.0.0.
